title: Rapid Development of Cell State Identification Circuits with Poly-Transfection
protocol: Ensure that the culture of human embryonic kidney (HEK293) cells is 60%-80% confluent before initiating the protocol.
Seed 1 x 10^6 cells in a 100 mm x 15 mm tissue culture Petri dish 2 days prior to use.
Incubate seeded HEK293 cells at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Pre-warm at least 20 mL of a solution of Dulbecco's modified eagle medium (DMEM) with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 1% non-essential amino acids (NEAA) to 37 °C.
Pre-warm at least 2.4 mL of Trypsin and 2.4 mL of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) to 37 °C.
Pre-warm reduced serum medium to ~16 °C.
Aspirate and dispose of the current media from the HEK293 cell culture.
Dispense 2 mL of PBS onto the HEK293 cell culture to wash the cells.
Aspirate and dispose of the PBS.
Dispense 2 mL of Trypsin onto the HEK293 cell culture.
Place the Petri dish in an incubator at 37 °C for 3 min or until the cells no longer adhere to the dish.
Return the dish to the biosafety cabinet and dilute the cell solution by dispensing 8 mL of DMEM solution into the plate.
Mix the solution by gently pipetting up and down several times.
Aspirate all the media and place it in a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 x g for 3 min to pellet them.
Aspirate the media (taking care not to aspirate the cells) and discard it.
Resuspend the cells in 5 mL of DMEM solution, mixing by gently pipetting up and down.
Estimate the current cell concentration using an automated cell counter.
Seed six wells in a 24-well plate with 1 x 10^5 cells (for a seeding density of 50,000 cells/cm²).
Add the DMEM solution up to 500 µL.
Label one well per treatment as no color control, mKO2 control, TagBFP control, NeonGreen control, all color control, and poly-transfection 1.
Add 36 μL of reduced serum medium to the no color control tube.
Add 36 μL of reduced serum medium to the mKO2 control tube.
Add 36 μL of reduced serum medium to the TagBFP control tube.
Add 36 μL of reduced serum medium to the NeonGreen control tube.
Add 36 μL of reduced serum medium to the all color control tube.
Add 18 μL of reduced serum medium to the poly-transfection mix 1 tube.
Add 18 μL of reduced serum medium to the poly-transfection mix 2 tube.
Add 600 ng of filler plasmid to the no color control tube.
Add 300 ng of mKO2 and 300 ng of filler plasmid to the mKO2 control tube.
Add 300 ng of TagBFP and 300 ng of filler plasmid to the TagBFP control tube.
Add 300 ng of constitutive NeonGreen plasmid and 300 ng of filler plasmid to the NeonGreen control tube.
Add 100 ng each of mKO2, TagBFP, and constitutive NeonGreen, as well as 300 ng of filler plasmid, to the all color control tube.
Add 150 ng of mKO2 to the poly-transfection mix 1 tube.
Add 75 ng of reporter NeonGreen plasmid and 75 ng of filler plasmid to the poly-transfection mix 1 tube.
Add 150 ng of TagBFP to the poly-transfection mix 2 tube.
Add 75 ng of L7ae plasmid and 75 ng of filler plasmid to the poly-transfection mix 2 tube.
Create a transfection master mix in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube by combining 216 μL of reduced serum medium with 9.48 μL of transfection reagent.
Mix well by pipetting up and down.
Add 1.58 µL of enhancer reagent to each no color control tube.
Add 1.58 µL of enhancer reagent to each single color control tube.
Add 1.58 µL of enhancer reagent to each all color control tube.
Add 79 µL of enhancer reagent to each poly-transfection mix tube.
Mix each tube individually by pipetting vigorously.
Add 37.58 µL of transfection master mix to each no color control tube.
Add 37.58 µL of transfection master mix to each single color control tube.
Add 37.58 µL of transfection master mix to each all color control tube.
Mix each tube individually by pipetting vigorously.
Add 18.79 µL of transfection master mix to each poly-transfection mix tube.
Mix each tube individually by pipetting vigorously.
Dispense 65.97 µL of each transfection mix for the no color, single color, and all color controls into corresponding wells.
Pipette 32.98 µL of poly-transfection mix 1 into the poly-transfection well.
Swirl the plate quickly but gently in a tight figure-eight pattern along a flat surface to distribute the complexes effectively.
Pipette 32.98 µL of poly-transfection mix 2 into the same poly-transfection well.
Swirl the plate again in the same fashion.
Place the plate in an incubator at 37 °C, with 5% CO2 and without shaking, for a period of 48 h.
Mix 300-600 ng of DNA with the appropriate volume of reduced serum medium for each control or poly-transfection tube.
Include an extra 10-20% volume of reduced serum medium to account for pipetting losses.
Mix 1.58 μL of P3000 per control tube.
Mix 0.79 μL of P3000 per poly-transfection tube.
Add 36 μL of reduced serum medium per control tube for Lipo master mix.
Add 18 μL of reduced serum medium per poly-transfection tube for Lipo master mix.
Mix 1.58 μL of transfection and enhancer reagent per control tube.
Mix 0.79 μL of transfection and enhancer reagent per poly-transfection tube.
Pre-warm at least 4.2 mL of the DMEM solution to 37 °C.
Pre-warm at least 4.2 mL of Trypsin and 4.2 mL of PBS to 37 °C.
Keep fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) buffer solution at 4 °C until ready to use.
Resuspend cells in FACS buffer solution as described below.
Aspirate and dispose of the current media in each well.
Dispense 5 mL of PBS into each well to wash the cells.
Aspirate and dispose of the PBS.
Dispense 5 mL of Trypsin into each well.
Place the plate in an incubator at 37 °C for 3 min, or until the cells no longer adhere to the dish.
Return the plate to the biosafety cabinet and dilute cell solutions by dispensing 5 mL of DMEM solution into each well.
For each well, mix the solution by gently pipetting up and down several times.
For each well, aspirate all the media and place it in a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 x g for 3 min to pellet them.
Aspirate the media, taking care not to aspirate the cells and discard it.
Resuspend the cells in 5 mL of FACS buffer solution by gently pipetting up and down.
Pass each cell suspension through a strainer into separate flow cytometry conical tubes.
Keep the tubes on ice for no more than 1 h.
Perform flow cytometry as soon as possible.
Look at single color controls.
Use all color control to tune instrument voltages for normalization of fluorescent protein signals to equivalent arbitrary units (a.u.) of fluorescence.
Run single color controls for each fluorescent protein to set the compensation matrix for bleed-through correction.
Ensure full dynamic range visibility for fluorescence values.
Consider running rainbow calibration beads for conversion to standardized units like molecules of equivalent fluorescein (MEFLs).
Run poly-transfection sample tube, ideally with 1,000 x 10^6 cells to ensure sufficient cell number per bin for statistical significance.
Use data from controls and beads during post-experiment analysis to ensure accurate results.
Perform live cell gating using predefined gates.
Apply compensation settings in the software.
Correct for autofluorescence.
